narrative.overview: ContractFlow is designed like a well-kept financial journal. Every number has its place, every transaction leaves a clear trail, and nothing is decorative. The system conveys precision, security, and absolute control.
keyCharacteristics: Clean slate surfaces with subtle structure
Cards lift on interaction — a tactile response, not a decorative flourish
Serif headings for authority; sans body for readability
Status communicated through color — the only place color carries semantic weight
No decoration that doesn't serve a task

rules.name: The Semantic Restraint Rule
rules.body: Color carries meaning or it doesn't appear. Peach = action, teal = navigation, green = active, yellow = paused, blue = complete, coral = danger. No decorative color use.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only saturated interactive color. It appears on links and interactive indicators only.

rules.name: The Single Source Rule
rules.body: All body copy and UI labels use Source Sans 3. Open Sans is exclusively for the navbar brand text. Source Serif 4 is exclusively for headings. No mixing within a role.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Every surface starts at rest with no shadow. Shadows appear only as a response to hover state.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one shadow in the system — the card hover. No modal shadows, no dropdown shadows, no tooltip shadows.

dos: Use the Warm Peach primary for all primary CTAs to maintain consistent action affordance.
Use Teal for all links so the user instantly recognizes interactive text.
Keep the card grid responsive with repeat(auto-fill, minmax(300px, 1fr)).
Use semantic tags (green/yellow/blue/coral) for status — they're the only color that carries meaning.
Batch actions behind an 'Actions' dropdown on detail views to keep the header clean.
Lead every page with a title and breadcrumb trail so the user always knows where they are.
Follow the budget-first flow: show estimates alongside actuals on every financial view.
donts: Don't use the primary peach as a background fill or decorative element — it's reserved for buttons and CTAs.
Don't add colored left borders to cards as accents (side-stripe border anti-pattern).
Don't use gradient text anywhere — all headings are solid colors.
Don't add glassmorphism, blurred surfaces, or decorative overlays.
Don't replicate the numbered section eyebrow (01 / 02 / 03) pattern — the landing page's 'How it Works' steps are a genuine sequence, not scaffolding.
Don't reinvent standard form controls — Bulma's .input, .select, .checkbox, and .file are the vocabulary.
Don't use modals as the first solution for create/edit flows — inline and progressive disclosure are better.
Don't add a card grid where the cards are all identical (icon + heading + text) — vary layout by content.
Don't use tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above every section.
Don't look like traditional accounting software: no dense gray grids, no jargon-heavy labels, no overwhelming dashboards.
